04aa70b7fd.q: What does Colleen O'Connell Campbell mean by the asset behind the asset in business exits?
04aa70b7fd.a: A business is rarely one asset but a bundle of assets—some obvious, some hidden, some financial, some emotional, some transferable, and some trapped inside the founder's head. To achieve a cash-rich exit, founders must understand what they own, what can transfer, what a buyer would value, and what is fragile, because the exit will reveal these gaps.

42d346dbfa.q: What did Joanna Trax of Good Eggs and Co. teach about owning versus renting business assets?
42d346dbfa.a: Joanna Trax emphasized the danger of building only on platforms you do not control and relying solely on algorithms. Instead, founders should build owned assets: email lists, websites, brand voice, customer relationships, content libraries, intellectual property, and community. Followers are not always transferable, and a social audience is not always an owned asset.

410a318524.q: How did Julie Cole's Mabel's Labels demonstrate the value of brand, community, and operations in a business exit?
410a318524.a: Mabel's Labels was not only a label company but an e-commerce business, community business, parenting brand, and trusted voice. When Avery Labels acquired the company, the buyer was purchasing the customer relationships, repeatability, trust, systems, and brand equity—not just the product. The asset behind the product is why customers keep coming back.

8f3e073271.q: Why did Dr. Lindy emphasize that product is not the same as a business in Essay Jacks' exit?
8f3e073271.a: Dr. Lindy built Essay Jacks, an ed tech company later acquired by WisePro, and learned that loving the product, service, and mission is different from building a business. A business requires attention to sales, financial modeling, go-to-market strategy, partnerships, metrics, legal structure, data, systems, and cash flow. The engine around the idea creates value, not just the idea itself.

6c3803a9a3.q: What structural requirements do Jennifer Williams and Tierra Letourneau identify for employee ownership models?
6c3803a9a3.a: Jennifer Williams of an Employee Design Group and Tierra Letourneau discussing Employee Ownership Trusts both emphasize that ownership without structure is a wish, not a plan. Governance, financial literacy, roles, leadership, transparency, evaluation, due diligence, financing, succession planning, trustees, and leadership readiness must all be in place. The legal structure cannot replace weak substance.
